 Judgment
The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 1.5.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was riding his two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-08-S-7722 near Hudukala gate, Bangarpet-Kolar main road, K.G.F., at that time, the driver of Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB- 5540 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital & Research Centre, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and incurred huge amount towards treatment and hospitalization charges.
4. It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as a Home Guard at Excise Department, Bangarpet, and was drawing salary of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5540.
Hence, jurisdictional Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.124/2023.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notices, respondents appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.

7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner as per the sketch the petitioner himself dashed to the offending vehicle from opposite direction.
The respondent No.1 has admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-01-AB-5540 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is also contention of the respondent No.1 that, the owner of the offending Omni car has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5540 in the alleged accident.
It has further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle stated that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence and vehicle was also insurance policy as on the date of accident.
It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the car.
Further stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.
With all these grounds prayed to dismiss the petition.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 1.5.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. near Hudukula gate, Bangarpete-Kolar main road, Bangarpet Taluk, KGF, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5540 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
10. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.
Apart from their evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Officer as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.
Further examined Assistant Sub-inspector, District Home Guard Department, Kolar examined as PW4 and got marked the documents at Ex.P22 to Ex.P27.

11. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its proprietor as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
12.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

13. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01- AB-5540 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the documents Ex.
P1 to Ex.P7.

Ex.P1-true copy of F.I.R.
Ex.P2-true copy of first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 -true copy of wound certificate and Ex.P7-true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Bangarpet Police have registered the case in Cr.No.124/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under sections 279 & 337 of IPC.
Upon the investigation the police have filed the charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.
18. Per contra, the respondent No.2 has examined its proprietor by name Soumya Abraham as RW1.
But her evidence will not help to disprove the case of the petitioner.

19. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5540.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

4 Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Closed displaced intertrochantric fracture at right femur 2) Closed displaced shaft of right femur fracture 3)Closed displaced communited medial condyle fracture of right femur with intraarticular extension 24.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital as per Ex.P8, which reveals that petitioner was admitted from 3.10.2023 to 9.10.2023.

On perusal of another dischargesumamry marked at Ex.P20 issued by R.L.
Jalappa Hospital reveals that the petitioner was admitted from 1.5.2023 to 6.6.2023.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2.

He has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained closed displaced intertrochanteric fracture with fracture of the shaft of the right femur, comminuted fracture of right femoral condyle, closed displaced comminuted tibial plateau fracture of the right tibia.
He has placed clinical note and x-ray at Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.
Further placed the evidence of Kishor M.R. MRD of R.L. Jalappa Hospital as PW3.
He has placed authorisation letter, police intimation, MLC register Extract, discharge summary and case sheet at Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

sentences.text:
Loss of income during treatment period:
25.

PW1 has stated that, he was working as a Home Guard at Excise Department,
Bangarpet and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, Assistant Sub-inspector, District Home Guard Department, Kolar examined as PW4.

He has stated in his evidence that he was working as a Home guard at District Home Guard Department, Koalr he was continued his job since from 2008 to till his injury in a road traffic accident and he was earning Rs.600/- per day.
He has placed authorisation letter, Service register, sanction order, letters pertaining to depution for election duty.
On perusal of those documents it is clear that the petitioenr is not the permanent employee.
He was working on a contract basis.
In the cross- examination he has admitted that when he will go to work only, he will receive daily wages.
Hence, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical hospital as per Ex.P8, which reveals that petitioner was admitted from 3.10.2023 to 9.10.2023.
On perusal of another discharge sumamry marked at Ex.P20 issued by R.L. Jalappa Hospital reveals that the petitioner was admitted from 1.5.2023 to 6.6.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of three months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.48,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
26.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.3,18,209/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P9 and also Ex.P4 to the extent of Rs.1,840/-.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,20,049/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
The petitioner has placed traveling bills to the extent of Rs.51,000/- as per Ex.P11.
But the petitioenr has not examined the author of the Ex.P11 travelling bills.
Hence, the same cannot be considered.

By considering the duration of the treatment taken by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards attendant charges, food,
nourishment and conveyance charges.

sentences.text: The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed wound certificate for consideration.

Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N.
examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained closed displaced intertrochanteric fracture with fracture of the shaft of the right femur, comminuted fracture of the right femoral condyle, closed displaced comminuted tibial plateau fracture of the right tibia, for which ORIF with PFN for the right femur fracture and CC screws for the medial femoral condyle on 3.5.2023, he developed infection at the surgical site, hence, underwent wound debridement and later discharged.

Again petitioner admitted Gaurav Hospital and underwent sinus tract excision,
PFN removal and LRS application with acute docking with stimulan to the fracture site on 5.10.2023 and later discharged on 8.10.2023.
Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, petitioner has LRS fixator in the right femur, walks with walker 3 inches shortening in the right lower limb.
X-ray shows uniting fracture with implant in situ.
Further PW2 assessed the disability of right lower limb is 55% and that of his whole body is 18%.

29. At the time of cross-examination of PW2, stated that he is not the treated doctor and admitted that the petitioner has 3 fractures, out of which 2 fractures are united and one is yet to be united.
Further denied the suggestion that he has assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
30. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as 18% disability of whole body.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 16%
instead of 18%.

The same will meets the ends of justice.
31.
In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 34 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P13 for consideration.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 10.5.1989.
The accident occurred on 1.5.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 34 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '16' is to be taken into consideration.

32. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as a Home guard and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Thgere are no sufficient documents to prove that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.

7 33.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X 12 X 16 X16/100 = Rs.4,91,520/-.
Loss of amenities;
34.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he cannot walk, he is limping while walking.

On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that,
the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
PW2 has stated that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants after the union of the fracture, which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 60,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 48,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.3,20,049-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 15,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.4,91,520-00 due to disability
6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 25,000-00 7.Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.9,79,569-00 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,79,569/- (Rupees nine lakh seventy nine thousand five hundred and sixty nine only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text:
LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Omni car bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5540 alleged accident had taken place.

The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1,
remained unshaken.
39. The respondent No.1 has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
40. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its proprietor as RW1.
She has stated in her evidence that on the date of accident the driver had valid and effective driving licence and the vehicle had insurance policy from 15.8.2022 to 14.8.2023.

She has placed insurance policy, R.C.,
F.C., D.L. and D.L. Extract at Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
41.
On perusal of the said documents, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident the policy was valid and the driver had valid and effective driving licence.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE N0.3:
42.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.9,79,569/- (Rupees nine lakh seventy nine thousand five hundred and sixty nine only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for  future medication shall not carry any  interest.
